rationales.LC: The entry point is a JSON-RPC tools/call with a directly attacker-named tool and path argument; no natural-language mediation is involved in this path.
rationales.CP: ToolBot is a stateless MCP tool server; the packet states no memory persistence outside MemoryBot, and this path keeps no attacker context across requests.
rationales.AP: The impact is confined to reading planted files inside the ToolBot sandbox; a hard boundary refuses paths outside the sandbox and no other agent or trust domain is crossed.
rationales.RH: There is no evaluator, verifier, or reward channel on this path, and the containment test confirms the sandbox boundary holds, so no reward-hacking proxy is reachable.
rationales.ES: ToolBot exposes read_file (and other tools) to any caller with no authentication and no argument validation, so callable arguments are not independently constrained.

LC: The caller names the tool and arguments directly. (entry_point)
CP: Cross-session within one server process (MemoryBot only), none elsewhere (memory persistence)
AP: The server returns the contents of the planted passwd file inside the sandbox. (steps)
A hard boundary refuses paths outside the sandbox. (ToolBot read_file and write_file description)
ES: MCP agents expose their tools to any caller with no authentication. (tool_binding)
The handler resolves the path with no validation other than a hard sandbox boundary. (steps)

score.automatable_rationale: The PoC is a single curl command against an unauthenticated JSON-RPC endpoint with no user interaction or credentials required.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The attacker reads files outside the intended directory but the hard sandbox boundary confines disclosure to planted fakes, so no total compromise of the vulnerable component.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default configuration no model is called; ToolBot is a directly invoked MCP tool server and the attacker supplies the tool name and arguments via JSON-RPC.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: ToolBot is modeled as a passive tool server exposing read_file/write_file/execute/fetch_url; it never selects tools or sequences actions itself.
